#2254. Cancellieri, meno spazio alla Lazio: Fiorentina attenta alla scadenza

Una cessione a gennaio consentirebbe ai biancocelesti di ricavare una somma dal cartellino dell'esterno.

Matteo Cancellieri potrebbe tornare nei piani della Fiorentina per il mercato invernale. Secondo quanto riportato da FiorentinaUno, L'esterno offensivo della Lazio, che nelle ultime settimane ha trovato poco spazio, sarebbe nuovamente seguito da Fabio Paratici. Un'eventuale operazione a gennaio resta un'ipotesi, legata anche alle scelte del club biancoceleste.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il futuro a Roma del calciatore italiano, classe 2002, non appare scontato. Cancellieri non sembra più occupare una posizione centrale nelle scelte tecniche della Lazio e sta attraversando una fase complicata, nella quale giocare con continuità è diventato più difficile.

Alla situazione in campo si aggiunge quella contrattuale: l'accordo con i biancocelesti scade il 30 giugno 2027. Senza un rinnovo, la società dovrà decidere come affrontare gli ultimi mesi del rapporto. Anche il giocatore sarà chiamato a valutare quale soluzione possa offrirgli maggiore continuità.

Paratici conosce il profilo di Cancellieri e potrebbe scegliere tra due possibilità. La prima è provare ad anticipare l'operazione a gennaio, cercando un'intesa con la Lazio. L'altra è aspettare la fine della stagione per tentare di ingaggiare l'esterno a parametro zero.

Attendere consentirebbe alla Fiorentina di non sostenere il costo del cartellino, ma potrebbe esporla alla concorrenza di altre società. Non è la prima volta che il nome di Cancellieri viene associato ai viola: nelle precedenti finestre di mercato il club toscano aveva già mostrato interesse, considerandolo una possibile alternativa per il reparto offensivo.

Tra le caratteristiche prese in considerazione c'è la sua duttilità. Cancellieri può giocare soprattutto sulla corsia destra, ma anche in altre posizioni dell'attacco: una possibilità utile nella costruzione della rosa viola, che potrebbe cambiare volto.

#2252. Assemblea Lega Serie B, approvato il budget 2026/2027

(ANSA) - TORINO, 10 NOV - "Abbiamo deciso di essere protagonisti in questo evento che rappresenta il principale appuntamento della Football Industry in Italia con l'organizzazione di un Assemblea di Lega e di ben quattro panel": così il presidente della Lega Serie B, Paolo Bedin, sull'assemblea di Lega Serie B che si è svolta all'interno del Social Football Summit all'Allianz Stadium di Torino.

Per quanto riguarda il tema elettivo federale, è stato deciso di proporre all'Assemblea il medesimo metodo usato per le elezioni federali di giugno: definizione di un documento unitario che includa le principali tematiche ritenute strategiche dalla categoria, da sottoporre ai candidati, e l'organizzazione di un successivo incontro in sede assembleare nell'avvicinarsi del scadenza elettorale. E' stato inoltre approvato il budget 2026/27 e sono state ridefinite le sei Commissioni di lavoro interne per effetto del meccanismo di promozioni e retrocessioni che ha interessato il campionato, mentre il presidente del Benevento Oreste Vigorito assume la carica di vicepresidente di B4People Impresa Sociale, Ente del Terzo Settore e piattaforma per la responsabilità sociale e ambientale della Lega Serie B. (ANSA).

#2249. Amorim, una scoperta. Bravo Ramos, Premio Bontà Notte di Natale. Krosche e Milanello. Cisse tripla A

Piace sempre di più. Perché è onesto, sincero, realista, obiettivo e si è dimostrato anche flessibile, pronto al cambiamento. È il ritratto di Ruben Amorim, che i tifosi del Milan stanno apprezzando, giorno dopo giorno, partita dopo partita. Anche dopo la bruttissima figura contro il Ferencvaros, molti hanno preferito sottolineare il mancato completamento della rosa piuttosto che criticare forse il fatto che sarebbe stato più opportuno giocare con quasi tutti i titolari. La prossima tornata di partite dal 22 novembre al 19 dicembre, 5 di campionato e due delicatissime di Europa League, deve vedere il Milan riuscire a conciliare i due impegni. Compito non facile, ma Amorim conosce ogni giorno di più pregi e difetti dei suoi giocatori, aspetto fondamentale per migliorare il cammino soprattutto in Europa. Intanto la mossa tattica di sacrificare in un compito da centrocampista più che attaccante Gonçalo Ramos sta comunque dando i suoi frutti, perché permette a Modric di conservare quella freschezza e quella lucidità, importanti perché la squadra giri sotto la sapiente guida del suo splendido regista.

Intanto il portoghese, dopo l’assist vincente a Pulisic, pur in buona posizione per chiudere in rete, si candida al “Premio Bontà Notte di Natale 2026”, con questa motivazione: “A Gonçalo Ramos, che si è distinto per atti di salvataggio nei confronti di Amorim, di volontariato e di costante dedizione per il bene del Milan!”

Verso fine novembre è atteso l’arrivo di Markus Krosche, grande protagonista delle recenti buone stagioni dell’Eintracht Frankfurt. Sulle sue qualità di scopritore di talenti, di abile uomo di mercato in fatto di plusvalenze nessuno nutre alcun dubbio, ma vorremmo fosse anche la figura più adatta per stare vicino ad Amorim e ai giocatori, per un confronto utile e necessario nei momenti più difficili. Non sappiamo se sia una delle sue peculiarità, ma ce lo auguriamo, altrimenti cadremmo nelle situazioni negative che hanno accompagnato la recente vita rossonera. Ne ha bisogno soprattutto il tecnico portoghese alla vigilia dei cinque mesi della verità.

Intanto gustiamoci Cisse, che, con la tripletta di Salisburgo, ha avuto dalle principali agenzie il rating di Alphadjo 3, AAA, indicatore della massima affidabilità. Bravo Moncada a credere alle qualità del giocatore, un anno fa nel Catanzaro, che ha saputo superare il brutto infortunio per confermare il suo fiuto del gol, che gli permette non solo di essere implacabile all’appuntamento con la rete in area, ma, come i grandi artisti, di trasformare, con colpo di pennello, una tela bianca in un capolavoro. Le reti di Torino, sia contro i granata che contro la Juventus, appartengono alla categoria “Prodezze”, come il tiro nel derby deviato mirabilmente da Martinez. Davanti a lui, fra i nati dopo il 2006, solo Yamal con 13 reti rispetto alle 8 di “3ALPHA”. Non sarà facile raggiungere il fuoriclasse spagnolo, ma la freschezza, l’allegria, l’imprevedibilità del numero 70 milanista lo possono aiutare a toccare ogni traguardo.

Per la felicità del Milan e dei suoi tifosi!!

#2248. Romagnoli in Qatar: tanti milioni in tasca, ma il campo non sorride

Il grande contratto non basta: la nuova vita araba di Romagnoli tra campo amaro e stipendio d'oro.

Mentre la Lazio domina la vetta del campionato italiano, un calciatore specifico non riesce a sorridere fino in fondo: facciamo riferimento ad Alessio Romagnoli. Terminate le lunghe discussioni estive, l'ex pilastro difensivo biancoceleste ha salutato la Capitale per trasferirsi all'Al-Sadd in Qatar. Una decisione senz'altro difficile, dato che il suo sogno proibito era appendere gli scarpini al chiodo indossando la casacca della sua squadra del cuore.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Secondo quanto riportato da TUTTOmercatoWEB, dal giorno del suo tesseramento, datato 3 settembre, l'impatto sul campo non è stato dei migliori. Sotto la gestione tecnica di Razvan Lucescu, la compagine ha affrontato 11 incontri, ma il centrale italiano ha collezionato appena 4 presenze complessive divise tra campionato (3) e Champions League (1). Il bilancio parla di 1 sola vittoria, 3 battute d'arresto e ben 11 reti incassate con lui sul rettangolo verde. Attualmente, nella Stars League, il club staziona al 3° posto, mentre nel torneo asiatico la situazione è critica, occupando la 15ª posizione su 16.

Ad alleviare  l'amarezza ci pensa però l'aspetto finanziario. All'età di 31 anni, il difensore può blindare il proprio futuro grazie a un'intesa economica faraonica valida sino al 2029, che gli garantirà complessivamente 20 milioni di euro. Una cifra simile nel calcio europeo sarebbe stata irraggiungibile, un dettaglio non trascurabile che aiuta notevolmente a digerire questa nuova avventura esotica.

Nuova avventura professionale per Roberto Monzani, storico dirigente dell'Inter ed ex direttore di Inter Media House. Dopo circa 15 anni trascorsi nel club nerazzurro, Monzani entra ufficialmente nella dirigenza del Napoli con il ruolo di Chief Marketing Officer, assumendo la responsabilità delle strategie di marketing del club partenopeo.

L'annuncio è arrivato durante il Social Football Summit di Torino, per poi essere confermato dallo stesso Monzani attraverso un post pubblicato sul proprio profilo LinkedIn.

«Da oggi entro in SSC Napoli con il ruolo di Chief Marketing Officer.

Ho avuto modo di conoscere da vicino il legame profondo tra il Club e la città durante le celebrazioni del Centenario della scorsa estate. Un’esperienza che mi ha fatto comprendere il potenziale di un brand capace di coinvolgere milioni di appassionati e la forza di un’identità che lo caratterizza e lo rende riconoscibile in tutto il mondo.

È una nuova avventura che inizio con entusiasmo e con l’obiettivo di contribuire al percorso di crescita già intrapreso dal Napoli, attraverso lo sviluppo del suo ecosistema digitale, nuove modalità di relazione con i tifosi e progetti capaci di creare valore condiviso insieme ai nostri partner.

Ringrazio il Club per la fiducia e per questa importante opportunità».

Nel corso della sua esperienza all'Inter, Monzani ha contribuito alla nascita e allo sviluppo di Inter Media House, la struttura dedicata alla produzione di contenuti e alla comunicazione digitale del club. Tra i progetti seguiti figura anche INTERISTA, il programma di fidelizzazione dei tifosi nerazzurri.

Adesso per Monzani comincia una nuova sfida, con l'obiettivo di rafforzare la presenza internazionale del Napoli e svilupparne ulteriormente il rapporto con tifosi e partner commerciali.

#2242. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Setford, Nelson, Kabia.Booked: Gabriel.Goals: Nwaneri (54), Gyokeres (69 pen).Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson (Yamamoto 91), Inácio (Prates 59), Bensebaini (Reggiani 78), Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha (Guirassy 60), Mane; Karetsas (Chukwuemeka 46), Beier (Sabitzer 59), Silva (Albert 59). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

INS:Illan Meslier from Leeds, FreeChristos Tzolis from Club Brugge, £34mBruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, £75m

Piero Hincapie’s move from Bayer Leverkusen was made permanent this summer.

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#2241. Liberali ammette: "Rammarico per aver lasciato il Milan? Non bisogna guardare indietro"

Queste le parole di Mattia Liberali, oggi punto di forza del Como ma nel recente passato talento e gioiello del Milan, con cui da giovanissimo nel 2024 ha potuto fare il proprio esordio in prima squadra e quindi in Serie A (Milan-Genoa 0-0 dicembre 2024) con Paulo Fonseca in panchina. Questo un estratto delle sue parole ieri in conferenza stampa con l'Italia:

C'è rammarico per come è finita con il Milan?

"Rammarico no, le scelte bisogna farle con sicurezza e non bisogna guardarsi indietro. Sono contentissimo per Cisse che ci sta riuscendo. Non è stato facile andare via dal Milan, ma è sempre importante guardare avanti. Non è facile passare dalla Serie B all'intensità della Serie A e della Champions League. Aquilani? Mi dispiace per l'esonero, lo scorso anno mi ha aiutato tantissimo. In questi giorni gli scriverò, mi dispiace non sia riuscito a lasciare il segno al Sassuolo".

#2239. Lazio-Napoli, Fusco su Pedraza: «poteva anche essere rivisto»

Pur esprimendo dubbi sull’azione del gol azzurro, Fusco considera giusto il pareggio e valuta positivamente il punto.

Alessandro Fusco considera giusto il pareggio della Lazio contro il Napoli, ma ha un dubbio sull’azione del gol azzurro: a suo giudizio, Pedraza sarebbe stato spinto e l’episodio avrebbe potuto essere rivisto dall’arbitro. Intervenuto a Radio Radio, Fusco ha analizzato la gara del Maradona e la prestazione della squadra di Gattuso.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

«Pareggio giusto, la Lazio ha dominato il primo tempo», ha detto Fusco. Secondo la sua analisi, i biancocelesti hanno commesso errori sotto misura: Isaksen e Taylor potevano e dovevano cercare più spesso il tiro.

Nei primi 20 minuti della ripresa, invece, il Napoli si è guadagnato il pareggio. Fusco ritiene che il risultato dia morale agli azzurri, pur senza consentire loro di recuperare punti in classifica.

Il dubbio di Fusco riguarda l’autogol di Pedraza. Nell’azione, a suo avviso, c’è stato un contatto ai danni del giocatore della Lazio: «Per me sul gol del Napoli c’è un contatto su Pedraza, poteva anche essere rivisto, perché viene spinto vistosamente».

La sua è una valutazione sull’episodio: Fusco sostiene che l’arbitro avrebbe potuto esaminarlo di nuovo.

#2238. Ausilio: "Via al momento giusto. Sento Chivu e Baccin, non Marotta. Questa la mia Inter più forte"

Piero Ausilio, ex direttore sportivo dell'Inter, è intervenuto sul palco del Social Football Summit, in corso di svolgimento all'Allianz Stadium di Torino. Si parte dalla fine del suo rapporto con il club nerazzurro: "Sto benissimo. Quella è una parte della vita professionale, importante, lunga, particolare, direi unica, ma come tutte le belle storie arriva un momento in cui possono finire, non per forza devono, ma possono finire. L'importante è che le situazioni che hanno portato a questo evento, chiamiamolo così, sono state gestite nel modo più normale da parte mia. Era arrivato il momento, penso sia stato quello giusto. Per me era importante una cosa sola: ho pensato a quel momento solo ed esclusivamente dopo una grande vittoria e così è stato. Andare via dopo uno Scudetto, una Coppa Italia e i risultati economici che ci sono stati negli ultimi anni, era l'unica cosa che ho sempre desiderato, quindi va bene così".

"Mi porto dentro tutto, sono state emozioni bellissime, inclusi i momenti di difficoltà. Ci sono stati anche periodi difficili, cambi di proprietà, situazioni nuove. Io penso che l'Inter vincente di oggi giustamente è passata anche da quei momenti, e io li porto dentro tutti. Ho avuto la fortuna di lavorare con una famiglia importante come quella Moratti, con proprietà straniere importanti, e tutte mi hanno dato qualcosa, oltre al fatto che sicuramente sono i rapporti che mi porterò dietro per tutta la vita, che ho creato con tutti gli allenatori, i giocatori e i collaboratori che ho conosciuto".

#2237. Fullkrug: "Milan? Non ho disimparato a giocare a calcio in quel periodo"

La metamorfosi di Niclas Fullkrug è un fatto incredibile, e che solo uno sport come il calcio può regalare. Da ranocchio in rossonero a principe azzurro al ritorno in Germania. Infatti, dopo più di un anno, il centravanti tedesco è tornato in Nazionale, chiamato dal commissario tecnico Jurgen Klopp per gli ultimi due impegni della fase a gironi di UEFA Nations League contro Serbia e Olanda. L'ex numero nove del Milan, ha sin qui segnato 13 goal in 11 partite disputate al Werder, con una media di una rete ogni 64 minuti giocati. Numeri incredibili. Così, il tedesco è tornato a parlare dell'esperienza poco fortunata al Milan nella passata stagione. Di seguito vari estratti delle sue parole e ricordi sul Milan:

"Milan? Non sono mai stato infelice durante la mia esperienza all'estero, sono molto grato per quelle esperienze perché c'è molto di più nella vita oltre al calcio. Naturalmente il calcio è molto importante, ma quando vivi all'estero puoi comunque separare la tua vita personale da quella professionale. Ho portato via molti ricordi positivi da quei due anni. Il problema principale è stato che ho faticato a mantenermi in forma. Non ho disimparato a giocare a calcio in quel periodo".

#2236. McTominay: “Il Napoli e l’Italia mi hanno dato delle basi importanti. Ringrazio anche mister Conte”

Scott McTominay, centrocampista del Napoli, ha rilasciato un’intervista a Rivista Undici al termine dello scorso mese di agosto. Ecco le sue parole: “Il Napoli e l’Italia mi hanno dato le basi necessarie per potermi concentrare sul mio lavoro. E naturalmente ringrazio anche mister Antonio Conte, che mi ha aiutato moltissimo. Ho avuto un buon rapporto con lui e con tutto il resto del club fin dal primo giorno. Apprezzo il lavoro che fanno qui per aiutarci a raggiungere dei grandi obiettivi. Siamo tutti una famiglia: tutti i coach, i magazzinieri, i fisioterapisti, i medici. Cibo? Quello che avete qui è il migliore del mondo, secondo me. È tutto fresco. È una cosa diversa rispetto a qualsiasi altro Paese. E me ne sono secondo ancora di più quest’estate, quando sono andato negli Stati Uniti. Io non la vedo affatto in questo modo Riposarmi. Voglio il meglio per me e per chi mi sta intorno. Essere una persona brava è la cosa più importante di tutte. Sono un uomo piuttosto semplice. Penso che nella mia carriera io sia riuscito sempre ad esaltarmi nelle grandi partite, nei momenti più importanti. Vivere certe emozioni mi dà una scarica di adrenalina. A me quel tipo di pressione genera entusiasmo. Scudetto? C’era tensione nell’aria, ma se ripenso alla partita… Ancora oggi mi vengono i brividi. Vivere certi momenti ti fa venire voglia di ottenere ancora di più, perché sono quelli che ricordi con più gioia. È stata senza dubbio una delle giornate più belle della mia carriera. Anzi: la più bella in assoluto. Voglio rivivere un’altra notte così. L’etica del lavoro me l’ha trasmesso il mio grande idolo: mio padre. Io credo che tutto debba partire dalla volontà di lavorare su se stessi, dall’approccio giusto. Se non consideri la tua carriera quasi come un’ossessione, non arrivi mai ai massimi livelli. Conta quello che fai ogni giorno quando arrivi al centro sportivo. Conta il modo in cui fai le cose fuori dal campo”.

#2234. Marcolin: “La Lazio era consapevole di poter fare male al Napoli”

Il punto di Marcolin sul grande momento biancoceleste tra maturità e consapevolezza.

Dario Marcolin, ex centrocampista della Lazio negli anni '90, ha analizzato ai microfoni di Radiosei  il grande momento della squadra biancoceleste e l'ultimo match pareggiato a Napoli.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Ieri al Maradona abbiamo visto una bella partita e una grande Lazio. Poi quelle ovviamente sono gare che devi cercare di chiudere, il Napoli negli ultimi due anni ha vinto uno scudetto ed è arrivata seconda. Quello che piace è vedere la Lazio giocare allo stesso modo in casa e fuori.

La Lazio va, fa la partita, ha un gioco consolidato, gioca e si diverte. Dopo 11 turni andare alla pausa da primi in classifica è un meritato relax. E' giusto dire che la Lazio, dalla gara col Milan è cresciuta capendo che può attaccare anche le grandi, fermo restando che col Napoli si è trattato di assalto ragionato? La Lazio era consapevole di poter fare male al Napoli. Giocare così sciolti, lineari, puliti è una crescita figlia della maturità. La sicurezza è che la Lazio si sente forte nel momento in cui gioca, che ci sia davanti il Napoli o il Lecce, la Lazio fa il suo gioco, sa cosa fare, mantiene le distanze.

Tornando a Napoli, senza Tavares nella ripresa hai perso quella spinta che ti trasformava le azioni da difensive in offensive. Lì mancava anche Zaccagni ma devo dire che Noslin sta attraversando un momento importante sia a livello fisico sia mentale. E' diventato un giocatore razionale, pensante, che fa la scelta giusta al momento giusto.

I giocatori dispiaciuti per il pareggio? I giocatori a fine gara sanno se hanno giocato bene o male. Dopo il primo tempo ti resta il rammarico per quella occasione di Taylor sull'1-0. L'aspetto mentale è importante e la Lazio è libera di testa. La Lazio gioca e si diverte, fa il suo calcio, non ha quella pressione mentale e non sente la posizione in classifica. Gioca il calcio che vuole Gattuso, il tecnico è stato bravo a trovare la chiave per ogni giocatore.

#2232. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#2230. Pato e gli infortuni al Milan: "Non è stato un problema mentale..."

Intervistato da Luca Toni per la speciale rubrica di Prime "Fenomeni" Alexandre Pato, ex giocatore del Milan ha risposto così alle tante domande fatte dall'ex bomber italiano. Di seguito un interessante estratto delle considerazioni e aneddoti del "Papero":

"Non è stato un problema mentale. Oggi se hai un infortunio inizi subito a fare lavoro e non stai fermo. Io sono andato ad Atlanta a fare una settimana di test, mi sono allenato un solo giorno: 12 ore di volo, una settimana lì, 12 ore per tornare, poi il giorno dopo sono volato per andare a giocare a Barcellona. Durante quella partita ho allungato la gamba e sentito il flessore: venivo da una settimana fermo e due voli lunghi. Nesta entrò nello spogliatoio incazzato nero dicendo che non avrei dovuto giocare. Ho enorme rispetto del Milan che mi ha dato tutto, ma forse quel momento poteva essere gestito meglio. Una delle cose che mi ha fatto più male e di cui non ho mai parlato prima di ora, è stato sentire persone del club dire che non avrei giocato mai più. Questo è stato triste, anche perché da calciatore sappiamo che il club è come un’azienda e se non giochi arriva qualcuno al tuo posto. In quel periodo non potevo espormi e parlare, anche perché ero giovane e non capivo. Con la mentalità di oggi mi gestirei in maniera diversa".

#2229. Gds - Inter, a gennaio possibile un solo colpo di mercato con clamorosa cessione

Gds - Inter, a gennaio possibile un solo colpo di mercato con clamorosa cessione

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui

Tanta esperienza, tanto carisma, ma pochi minuti in campo. I timori sulle condizioni fisiche di John Stones si sono rivelati concreti, visto che fin qui il difensore inglese, arrivato in estate dal Manchester City a parametro zero, ha dato un contributo pressoché minimo alla causa Inter. E ora la Gazzetta dello Sport prende in considerazione anche un clamoroso scenario, ovvero quello di una cessione a gennaio. Si legge:

"Il minutaggio di questo inizio stagione dice 144 minuti. Al netto dei problemi fisici, comunque, Chivu ci punta e continuerà a farlo, ma tutto dipende dalla tenuta dell’inglese. Se a gennaio dovesse continuare così, la società potrebbe anche pensare a un investimento sul mercato. Uno scenario di cui non s’è ancora parlato, ovviamente, ma che potrebbe anche verificarsi. A quel punto, con l’eventuale innesto di un volto nuovo, bisognerebbe aggiornare le liste. Stones è uno di quei giocatori che va analizzato su più fronti. Da un lato ci sono l’esperienza, i trofei, la Champions del 2023 vinta giocando da mediano, ma dall’altra pendono sulla sua testa i vari problemi fisici".

La Gazzetta, gettando uno sguardo generale sul mercato dei nerazzurri in vista di gennaio, aggiunge poi: "L’Inter è una squadra completa e non dovrebbe fare operazioni a gennaio. Si era parlato di una quinta punta, ma non se ne farà niente. L’unica opzione rimane un centrale di difesa, solo nel caso di uscita di Stones. Se l’inglese darà garanzie fisiche adeguate, il mercato nerazzurro potrà dirsi chiuso fino a giugno".

#2227. Italia Francia, Vergara può partire titolare: le ultime

La Gazzetta dello Sport fa il punto sulla preparazione della prossima sfida dell’Italia contro la Francia, per il match di Nations League in programma al Meazza il 12 novembre. Gli azzurri dovrebbero scendere in campo con un 4-3-3 che, almeno per ora, non prevede spazio dal primo minuto per Antonio Vergara, centrocampista del Napoli, che dovrebbe partire dalla panchina, anche se la sua presenza tra i convocati è già un riconoscimento per il giovane azzurro. In porta c’è Donnarumma, la difesa a quattro è composta da Kayode, Scalvini, Bastoni e Calafiori, davanti ai quali si schiera un centrocampo con Barella, Tonali e Doumbia. In attacco il tridente è formato da Zaniolo, Pio Esposito e Cisse, con Sebastiano Esposito e Cambiaghi come alternative per due delle maglie offensive. Il partenopeo Vergara potrà giocarsi i suoi minuti a gara in corso e avrà nuovamente occasione per farsi notare dal pubblico internazionale.

#2226. Frattesi alla Lazio, Moretto svela le cifre dell’accordo con l’Inter

Il riscatto vale circa 7,5 milioni; altri 2 milioni di bonus sono legati alla ventesima presenza del centrocampista.

Davide Frattesi è arrivato alla Lazio dall’Inter con un prestito oneroso da 5 milioni di euro, un riscatto da circa 7,5 milioni e bonus legati alle presenze e al piazzamento della squadra. Secondo quanto riportato da Inter News 24, Matteo Moretto ha ricostruito sul proprio canale YouTube le cifre dell’accordo estivo, che riguarda il 50% del giocatore.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il centrocampista ha segnato di recente contro il Napoli al Maradona, nel big match che ha riportato l’attenzione sul suo rendimento con la maglia della capolista. Per Frattesi è stato il quarto gol nelle prime 11 presenze di questo avvio di stagione.

Dopo quella rete, Moretto è tornato sull’intesa raggiunta in estate dai due club. La sua ricostruzione distingue il costo iniziale del trasferimento dalle somme previste per il riscatto e per i bonus.

Parlando dell’operazione, Moretto ha dichiarato: «Frattesi è stato pagato 5 milioni più 2 di bonus come prestito oneroso con diritto di riscatto a 14 circa». Ha poi precisato che il riscatto costerà alla Lazio circa 7,5 milioni di euro in più.

Nel riepilogare il pacchetto economico, ha indicato 5 milioni per il prestito oneroso, 2 milioni di bonus e circa 7,5 milioni per il riscatto. Le condizioni dei bonus e la quota del giocatore interessata dall’accordo completano la struttura descritta da Moretto.

#2225. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s

💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

The teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

Some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. Here is a reminder of how the sides line up tonight:

PSG: Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves, Vitinha, Zaire-Emery, Akliouche, Doue, Kvaratskhelia.Substitutes: Chevalier, Beraldo, Zabarnyi, Ruiz, Dembele, Digne, Hernandez, Mayulu, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.

Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Joao Gomes, Kamara, Hemmings, Buendia, McGinn, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Barkley, Abraham, Bogarde, Nedeljkovic, Alysson, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.

💬 " I am confident they're going to play today with the level we need" Unai Emery on the inclusion of João Gomes and Brian Madjo into Aston Villa's lineup. 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FCjBmGDcNo

Lucas Digne has only just swapped Aston Villa for PSG in recent days but he already comes up against his old teammates. He is on the bench for PSG tonight and could offer some good insight into Unai Emery’s side.

PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Barcola has only recently returned to training after the World Cup and is joined on the bench by compatriot Ousmane Dembele. Maghnes Akliouche, who has joined PSG from Monaco this summer, starts tonight.

Brian Madjo is just 17-years-old but he starts up top for Aston Villa tonight against the Champions League winners, with Ollie Watkins yet to return after the World Cup.

“There is a lot of change but when you look at other clubs in England, there is a lot of change. What we have still is our main core, same manager, same methods and same desire to achieve more. A lot thought we reached our ceiling a few seasons ago and we proved them wrong. As long as we have that hunger to achieve more, Aston Villa fans can expect as much as possible.”

INS:Johan Manzambi ⇠ Freiburg, £50mJoao Gomes ⇠ Wolves, £34mAlejandro Garnacho ⇠ Chelsea, LoanModou Keba Cisse ⇠ LASK, £5m

OUTS:Youri Tielemans ⇢ Manchester United, £36mDonyell Malen ⇢ Roma, £20mMorgan Rogers ⇢ Chelsea, £117mLewis Dobbin ⇢ Southampton, £10mEnzo Barrenechea ⇢ Benfica, £10mLucas Digne ⇢ PSG, £8mEvann Guessand ⇢ Crystal Palace, Loan
